title: How do we understand differences?
text:
Some people think that friends should be alike, but some other people think that friends should be different.
What do you think?
Should friends be similar or different?

I think a good friend is like a mirror.
You can understand people by knowing their friends.
My friend, Stephen, is a great example.
We often hang out together because we have similar hobbies and interests.
For example, we both love sports.
He plays badminton better than I do, so he always wins our matches.
Because of that, I try harder when I practise, and now I'm getting better at badminton.

Stephen and I are similar in other ways.
He is as serious as me.
When we aren't playing sports, we enjoy reading together.
I read more history books than he does, and he reads a lot of novels.
We often share interesting books with each other.

I don't agree.
For me, friends who are different make me better.
I think we should respect each other's differences and learn from each other.
For example, I am kind of shy, but my best friend, Yuan Lei, is outgoing.
She has a great sense of humour too.
Thanks to her, I am becoming more outgoing.
Now I think meeting new people is really fun!

I have another friend, Zhang Yong.
He is not afraid to give his opinion, especially when he thinks I am making a mistake.
I am less straightforward than he is, but I am glad to have an honest friend.

I don't really care if my friends are similar to or different from me.
I have two amazing friends.
Lily is funnier than anyone else I know.
When I feel sad or have a problem, she makes me laugh and feel better.
She helps me see the silver lining in difficult situations.

My other friend, Lucy, is not as funny as Lily.
Lucy is quieter, but she listens better than others.
Lucy and I talk about everything.
I know she cares about me because she's always there to listen.

My favourite saying is, "A true friend reaches for your hand and touches your heart."
Both Lily and Lucy are true friends.
We are always ready to help each other by lending a hand.
textTranslate:
有些人认为朋友应该相像，另一些人却认为朋友应该不同。
你怎么认为？
朋友应该相像还是不同？

我认为好朋友就像一面镜子。
通过了解一个人的朋友，你可以了解这个人。
我的朋友斯蒂芬就是一个很好的例子。
我们经常一起玩，因为我们的爱好和兴趣相似。
例えば，我们都喜欢运动。
他羽毛球打得比我好，所以每次比赛他都赢。
因此，我练习时更加努力，现在羽毛球也打得越来越好了。

斯蒂芬和我在其他方面也很相似。
他和我一样严肃。
不做运动的时候，我们喜欢一起读书。
我读的历史书比他的多，他则读很多小说。
我们经常互相分享有趣的书。

我不同意。
对我来说，与自己不同的朋友能让我变得更好。
我认为我们应该尊重彼此的差异，互相学习。
比如，我有点害羞，但我最好的朋友袁蕾很外向。
她也很有幽默感。
多亏了她，我正在变得更加外向。
现在我觉得认识新朋友真的很有趣！

我还有另一个朋友张勇。
他敢于说出自己的看法，尤其是当他认为我犯错的时候。
我没他那么直率，但有一个诚实的朋友，我很高兴。

我并不在意朋友和我相像还是不同。
我有两个很棒的朋友。
莉莉比我认识的任何人都更幽默。
当我难过或遇到问题时，她会逗我笑，让我感觉好起来。
她帮助我在困境中看到一线希望。

我的另一个朋友露西没有莉莉那么幽默。
露西更文静，但她比其他人更善于倾听。
露西和我无话不谈。
我知道她关心我，因为她总是陪在我身边，听我说话。

我最喜欢的格言是：真正的朋友会向你伸出手，也会触及你的心灵。
莉莉和露西都是真正的朋友。
我们总是愿意互相帮助，伸出援手。

title: One Big Family
text:
China is a country made up of 56 different ethnic groups.
The Han Chinese, the largest group, live all over the country.
The other 55 ethnic groups live in different parts of China.
You can find them in Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region, Yunnan Province, and many other areas.

Each ethnic group has its own clothes, music, arts, and festivals.
They all contribute to Chinese culture.
The Chinese government works hard to make sure that all people live together in fairness and peace.
In China, students from all ethnic groups can learn about each other's cultures in school.
They can also watch TV programmes to understand how important it is to get along with and respect each other.

In China, all ethnic groups are like one big family.
They respect each other, learn from each other, and help each other.
When everyone works together, it makes China stronger and better.
textTranslate:
中国是由56个不同民族组成的国家。
汉族是最大的民族，生活在全国各地。
其他55个民族居住在中国不同的地区。
你可以在内蒙古自治区、云南省和其他许多地区找到这些民族。

每个民族都有自己的服饰、音乐、艺术和节日。
他们都为中华文化作出了贡献。
中国政府努力确保所有人都能在公平与和谐中共同生活。
在中国，各民族学生都可以在学校了解彼此的文化。
他们还可以观看电视节目，明白与他人和睦相处、彼此尊重有多么重要。

在中国，各民族就像一个大家庭。
他们彼此尊重、互相学习、互相帮助。
当大家齐心协力时，中国就会变得更强大、更好。

title: How are plants and animals connected with us?
titleTranslate: 植物和动物与我们有什么联系？
text:
Imagine you go to the supermarket in your area, but there are almost no fruits, vegetables, honey, milk, eggs, or chocolate.
How would you feel?
Disappointed?
Angry?
Sad?
At this moment you realize people, plants, and animals are all connected.
We need each other to live, and bees are one of the best examples of this connection.

Bees are very hard-working animals, and their greatest work is pollination.
On one trip, they often visit 50 to 100 flowers.
As they fly from one flower to another, they take pollen with them.
This action helps plants grow.
In fact, without their work, about 80 per cent of the plants in the world cannot grow.
For this reason, many scientists believe that bees are the most important animals on this planet.

Bees are also one of the most interesting animals in the world.
For example, they work hard together to make their homes.
In order to store honey, they create honeycombs.
Another interesting thing about bees is how they communicate.
When a bee finds new food, it uses a dance to tell the others where and how far away the food is.

Bees play an important part in the ecosystem of our planet.
However, the number of bees is dropping, and scientists are worried.
Bees need our help, and there is a lot we can do.
Think about what you can do to protect one of the most amazing animals on earth.

The blue whale is the largest and heaviest animal on earth.
It can weigh as much as 200 tons.
Many people like watching blue whales swim, and they think it is one of the most beautiful things to see.
Blue whales live in all oceans except the Arctic Ocean.
They eat a lot, but they eat some of the tiniest animals in the ocean.
A blue whale can eat around four tons of these a day.

Blue whales can live up to 90 years.
When a blue whale dies at sea, it becomes food for many kinds of animals living in and around the sea.
This food lasts for over a year and it helps to create a lively and healthy ecosystem.
Blue whales play an important role in our world, so we must protect them.
textTranslate:
想象一下，你去了家附近的超市，却几乎看不到水果、蔬菜、蜂蜜、牛奶、鸡蛋或巧克力。
你会感到怎么样？
失望？
生气？
伤心？
就在这时，你意识到人类、植物和动物都是相互依存的。
我们相互依存才能生存，蜜蜂就是这种依存关系最好的例证之一。

蜜蜂是勤劳的动物，它们最重要的劳作是授粉。
一次采蜜过程中，它们通常要拜访50到100朵花。
当它们从一朵花飞向另一朵花时，会随身携带花粉。
这一活动有助于植物生长。
事实上，如果没有它们的劳动，世界上约80%的植物就无法生长。
因此，许多科学家认为蜜蜂是这个星球上最重要的动物。

蜜蜂也是世界上最有意思的动物之一。
例如，它们齐心协力建造自己的家园。
为了储存蜂蜜，它们筑造蜂巢。
蜜蜂有趣的一点还在于它们的交流方式。
当蜜蜂发现新的食物时，它会通过舞蹈告诉其他蜜蜂食物在哪里以及有多远。

蜜蜂在地球生态系统中发挥着重要作用。
然而，蜜蜂的数量正在减少，科学家对此深感担忧。
蜜蜂需要我们的帮助，我们能做很多事。
想想你能做些什么，来保护地球上最惊奇的动物之一。

蓝鲸是地球上最大、最重的动物。
它的体重可达200吨。
许多人喜欢观看蓝鲸游泳，并认为这是世上最美的景象之一。
除北冰洋外，蓝鲸生活在所有海洋中。
它们吃得很多，但吃的是海洋中一些最小的动物。
一头蓝鲸一天可以吃掉大约四吨这类动物。

蓝鲸的寿命可达90年。
当蓝鲸在海中死去时，它会成为许多生活在海中及海边动物的食物。
这些食物可以维持一年多，有助于营造充满活力且健康的生态系统。
蓝鲸在世界上发挥着重要作用，因此我们必须保护它们。

title: A Folk Story of Zisu
text:
During the Eastern Han Dynasty, some rich young men were celebrating the Double Ninth Festival.
They had a competition at a restaurant to see who could eat the most crabs.
Hua Tuo, a well-known doctor, was also there.
He warned them not to do so.
He said crabs were "cooling" and eating too many could make them sick.
But the young men did not listen and kept eating more crabs.

Later that night, most of the young men got serious stomachaches.
They asked Hua Tuo for help.
Hua Tuo went out to the fields with his students.
They found a special purple plant and boiled its stems and leaves in water.
They made a herbal drink with the water and gave it to the sick young men.
After they drank it, their stomachaches went away.

Hua Tuo called the purple plant zishu, which means purple and comfortable.
In English, it is known as purple perilla.
Later, people called it zisu and it became a common Chinese herbal medicine.
textTranslate:
东汉时期，一些富家青年正在庆祝重阳节。
他们在一家餐馆比赛，看谁能吃下最多的螃蟹。
名医华佗也在场。
他劝他们不要这样做。
他说螃蟹性寒，吃得太多会使他们生病。
但这些青年没有听从劝告，还继续吃更多螃蟹。

当晚晚些时候，大多数青年都出现了严重的胃痛。
他们向华佗求助。
华佗和他的学生们一起去了田野。
他们找到一种特殊的紫色植物，把它的茎和叶放在水中煮沸。
他们用这些水制成一种草药饮料，给生病的青年喝。
喝下后，他们的胃痛就消失了。

华佗称这种紫色植物为“紫舒”，意思是紫色而舒适。
它的英文名称是紫色紫苏。
后来，人们称它为“紫苏”，它也成了一种常见的中草药。

title: How do we make food?

title: What does cooking give us?
titleTranslate: 烹饪能给我们带来什么？
text:
Through food and cooking we create memories and show love to others.
It is fun to learn how to make food from other cultures.
I have wonderful memories of my grandmother's kitchen.

"Cooking is love made visible."
That is what my grandmother always told me.
Thanks to her, I love cooking.
It's a great way for me to share my love with others.
Every time I sit at the table, after cooking for my family, we create memories.
The smells and the food's taste, along with our conversations, connect us to each other.
What wonderful memories I have!

One of my favourite memories is my grandmother's pumpkin pie.
She always made it in autumn, when the weather got colder.
Her friendly kitchen was the perfect place to warm up and enjoy a taste of the changing seasons.
I still remember the days when the smell of cinnamon filled the room with sweetness.
Now, every time I smell cinnamon, I think of my grandmother's pumpkin pie.

My grandmother told me about her first pumpkin pie.
When she was a college student in the US, she stayed with a host family.
One year around Thanksgiving, the hostess taught her how to make a pumpkin pie.
Many years later, she taught me how to make it too.

Ingredients: eggs, sugar, cinnamon, salt, pumpkin, cream, pie crust Instructions: First, mix the eggs.
Then, add the sugar, cinnamon, salt, pumpkin, and cream.
Next, pour the mixture into the pie crust.
After that, place the pie in the oven and cook for 40 to 50 minutes.
Finally, let the pie cool for at least an hour before serving.

My grandmother loved learning how to make food from other cultures.
"It's my way of making friends from around the world," she said.
Grandmother taught me the secret to cooking: Cook with love.
Thanks to my grandmother, I love to try new food and new recipes from other countries and cultures.

@thechinesechefblog Long ago, there was a couple living in Yunnan Province, China.
The husband studied on an island far from his home.
When his wife went a long way to send meals, the food always got cold.
One day, the wife boiled some chicken soup and used a large pot to keep it warm.
And she kept the ingredients separate.
She put the ingredients into the soup when she reached the island, and she found everything still hot.
The Guoqiao Rice Noodles was born!
textTranslate:
通过食物和烹饪，我们创造回忆，向他人表达爱。
学习制作其他文化的食物很有趣。
我对祖母的厨房有着美好的回忆。

“烹饪是看得见的爱。”
这就是祖母总是对我说的话。
多亏了她，我喜欢上了烹饪。
这是我与他人分享爱意的绝佳方式。
每当为家人做完饭，一家人围坐在餐桌旁，我们就会创造美好的回忆。
食物的气味和味道，以及我们的交谈，都让我们彼此更加亲近。
我拥有多么美好的回忆啊！

我最珍爱的回忆之一，是祖母做的南瓜派。
她总是在秋天天气转凉时做南瓜派。
她温馨的厨房是取暖、品尝时令变化的好地方。
我至今仍记得那些日子，空气中弥漫着肉桂的香气，满屋都是甜蜜的味道。
如今，每当我闻到肉桂的气味，就会想起祖母的南瓜派。

祖母曾给我讲述她做的第一个南瓜派。
她还在美国上大学时，曾寄宿在一个当地家庭。
有一年临近感恩节，女主人教她制作南瓜派。
多年以后，她也教我制作南瓜派。

配料：鸡蛋、糖、肉桂、盐、南瓜、奶油、派皮。制作方法：首先，把鸡蛋搅拌均匀。
然后，加入糖、肉桂、盐、南瓜和奶油。
接着，把混合物倒入派皮中。
然后，把南瓜派放进烤箱，烤40至50分钟。
最后，让南瓜派至少冷却一小时再食用。

祖母喜欢学习制作其他文化的美食。
她说：“这是我结识世界各地朋友的方式。”
祖母教给我烹饪的秘诀：用爱烹饪。
多亏了祖母，我喜欢品尝其他国家和文化的新食物，学习新菜谱。

@thechinesechefblog 很久以前，中国云南省有一对夫妻。
丈夫在远离家乡的一座岛上求学。
妻子每次长途跋涉给他送饭，饭菜到时总是已经凉了。
一天，妻子煮了一些鸡汤，并用一个 大锅保温。
她还把各种食材分开放。
到达岛上后，她才把食材放进汤里，发现所有东西仍然热腾腾的。
云南过桥米线就此诞生！

title: Tanghulu
text:
Tanghulu is a popular Chinese snack, especially in the winter in northern China.
It has different names in different places.
However, people make tanghulu in almost the same way.
First, they put hawthorn onto wooden sticks.
Then, they put them into hot sugar syrup.
As the syrup cools down and hardens, it creates a candy shell.
People also use other fruits, like oranges and strawberries, to make different types of tanghulu.

Tanghulu has a long history in China.
About 800 years ago, the emperor's wife was sick and couldn't eat or drink anything.
The palace doctors didn't know how to help her.
Later, a wise doctor came to the palace.
He prepared some hawthorn coated in sugar, and advised the empress to eat some before every meal.
A few days later, she felt better.
People heard the story and more and more people started making tanghulu at home.
textTranslate:
糖葫芦是中国广受欢迎的小吃，在中国北方尤其冬季常见。
它在不同的地方有不同的名称。
不过，人们制作糖葫芦的方法几乎相同。
首先，他们把山楂串在木签上。
然后，把山楂放进滚烫的糖浆中。
随着糖浆冷却并凝固，便形成了一层糖衣。
人们还使用其他水果，如橙子和草莓，制作不同种类的糖葫芦。

糖葫芦在中国有着悠久的历史。
约800年前，皇帝的妻子生病了，无法进食或饮水。
宫中的御医们不知道该如何帮助她。
后来，一位睿智的医生来到宫中。
他用糖裹了一些山楂，建议皇后在每餐前吃一些。
几天后，她感觉好多了。
人们听说这个故事后，越来越多的人开始在家制作糖葫芦。

title: How can we make good plans?
titleTranslate: 我们如何制定完善的计划？
text:
Although there are differences, most resolutions have one thing in common: People hardly ever keep them!
But there are good reasons for this.
Sometimes the resolutions may be too difficult to keep.
And sometimes people just forget about them.

As my birthday draws near, it is the perfect time to think about the changes I can make.
I can improve myself by learning something new, forming good habits, working harder at something, or even improving my relationships with others.
I hope to make my future life better than before, so I am going to make three resolutions.

The first one is about taking up a new hobby.
I am going to join the school music club to improve my singing!
I think singing is a great activity.
And my friends and family all love my singing.

I am also going to get fitter.
Besides jogging, I am going to do push-ups and sit-ups.
I feel energetic after I exercise.
I'm sure I'm going to be a healthier and happier person.

Last but not least, my English isn't good enough, so I am going to study for two more hours each weekend.
It might be hard, but I am going to get a lot better at English!
textTranslate:
尽管计划各不相同，但大多数计划都有一个共同点：人们几乎从不坚持到底！
但这是有充分理由的。
有时，计划可能太难坚持。
有时，人们只是把它忘了。

随着我的生日临近，正是思考自己可以作出哪些改变的好时机。
我可以通过学习新知识、养成好习惯、更加努力地做好某件事，甚至改善与他人的关系来提升自己。
我希望今后的生活比过去更好，因此我要制定三个计划。

第一个计划是培养一项新爱好。
我要参加学校音乐社，提高自己的唱歌水平！
我认为唱歌是一项很棒的活动。
而且，我的家人和朋友都喜欢听我唱歌。

我还要让自己变得更健康。
除了慢跑，我还要做俯卧撑和仰卧起坐。
运动后，我感到精力充沛。
我相信，自己一定会成为一个更健康、更快乐的人。

最后但同样重要的是，我的英语还不够好，因此我打算每个周末再学习两个小时。
这可能很难，但我一定会让我的英语水平提高很多！

title: Health Planning
text:
Many people around the world like to include "staying healthy" in their New Year's or birthday resolutions.
Some of them even make a year-long health plan.
People in different countries have their own ways of health planning.
Chinese people usually turn to Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM).

According to TCM, the first thing we need to do is to prevent health problems before they happen.
In this regard, TCM holds that lifestyle is closely connected to health, and we should take care of our health every day.
We can do this by managing our feelings, getting enough rest, eating well, and following good habits.

TCM is also helpful when we are sick.
It helps stop the sickness from getting worse.
And it prevents our body from losing too much energy.
After we get well, if we follow TCM advice, we can prevent the sickness from coming back, at least for a short time.
For example, after a fever, we are supposed to eat light food that is easier for our body to digest, so we can stay healthy for longer.
textTranslate:
世界各地很多人都喜欢把“保持健康”列入新年或生日愿望清单。
有些人甚至会制定一年的健康计划。
不同国家的人有各自规划健康的方式。
中国人通常会求助于中医。

根据中医理论，我们首先需要做的是在健康问题发生之前加以预防。
在这方面，中医认为生活方式与健康密切相关，我们应当每天关注自己的健康。
我们可以通过调节情绪、保证充足休息、合理饮食以及养成良好习惯来实现这一点。

中医在我们生病时也很有帮助。
它有助于防止病情恶化。
它还可以防止我们的身体消耗过多精力。
等我们康复后，如果遵照中医的建议，就能防止疾病再次复发，至少短时间内可以。
例如，发烧后应当吃清淡、易消化的食物，这样我们就能保持更长时间的健康。

title: How can we prepare for the future?
titleTranslate: 我们如何为未来做好准备？
text:
Host: Good evening, everyone!
Our guest today is Dr Lu Xingyuan, chief researcher of the Future World Research Centre.

Dr Lu: Good evening.
Thank you, it's a pleasure to be here.
Host: Dr Lu, thank you for joining us.
So, as a futurist, can you tell us how life will be different in 50 years?
Dr Lu: Well, you'll see robots working everywhere.
Host: Can you give us some examples?
Dr Lu: Well, as we all know, China's robotics industry is growing fast.
Robots will make our life easier.
We'll have service robots.
They will do almost all our housework.
They will also help save lives when disasters and emergencies happen.
Host: So, what jobs will humans still do in the future?
Dr Lu: Good question!
Some jobs today will disappear in the coming years.
However, there will be more challenging jobs in the future, such as space pilots and AI experts.
Host: Do you think robots will replace humans one day?
Dr Lu: No, I don't.
Our creativity and emotional intelligence are important for relationships.
AI will not replace humans for these things.
Host: You mentioned AI.
How will AI change our world?
Dr Lu: Well, it will certainly change how we work, study, and live.
For example, a smart refrigerator will know what you need and order food for you when you're running low.
Host: Wow, that'll save us a lot of time!
Now, my last question: How can we prepare for the future?
Dr Lu: It's simple.
Just accept change.
Keep learning and working hard.
Today's choices will influence your future.
Host: Thank you for your time, Dr Lu.

As an artist, I will live in the countryside and stay close to nature.
There will be flowers and plants around my home.
Life there will give me good ideas for making art.
At the weekend, I will invite friends to come over and have fun together.

I believe these dreams will come true as long as I study hard and keep on trying.

What will my life be like in 20 years?
It's not an easy question, but here are a few of my predictions.
I love art, so I think I will become an artist.
I want to study art in France, and then I will visit all the famous art museums.
I will learn a lot about different artists and their works of art, and I will create my own too.
textTranslate:
主持人：大家晚上好！

主持人：您能给我们举几个例子吗？

机器人会让我们的生活更加便捷。
我们将拥有服务机器人。
它们几乎可以承担我们所有的家务。
发生灾难和紧急情况时，它们也会协助挽救生命。
主持人：那么，未来人类还会从事哪些工作？
卢博士：这个问题问得好！
如今的一些工作在未来几年内会消失。
不过，未来会出现更多具有挑战性的工作，例如太空飞行员和人工智能专家。
主持人：您认为机器人终有一天会取代人类吗？
卢博士：不，我不会这样认为。
我们的创造力和情绪智力对于人际关系很重要。

主持人：您提到了人工智能。
人工智能将如何改变我们的世界？
卢博士：嗯，它肯定会改变我们的工作、学习和生活方式。
例如，智能冰箱会了解你的需求，并在食品即将用完时为你订购食物。
主持人：哇，这会为我们节省很多时间！
现在，我还有最后一个问题：我们该如何为未来做好准备？
卢博士：很简单。
只要接受变化。
不断学习，努力工作。
今天的选择将影响你的未来。
主持人：卢博士，感谢您抽出时间参加节目。

作为一名艺术家，我会住在乡村，亲近大自然。
我的家周围会有鲜花和绿植。
那里生活会给我带来艺术创作的好灵感。
周末，我会邀请朋友来家中一起玩耍。

只要我努力学习并坚持不懈，我相信这些梦想终会实现。

20年后，我的生活会是什么样？

我热爱艺术，所以我想成为一名艺术家。
我想去法国学习艺术，然后参观所有著名的艺术博物馆。
我会详细了解不同的艺术家及其艺术作品，也会创作自己的作品。

title: Smart Home
text:
In recent years, the idea of smart homes has become more and more popular in China.
Many large cities now hold smart home exhibitions where people can learn about new smart products and technologies.
They are gradually changing how people live, study, and even work at home.

To build a basic smart home, the first thing you usually need is a smartphone.
Next, connect your smart devices to the internet and install the necessary apps.
With everything ready, you can control many things more easily.

Today, many families, especially those in big cities, are already using some of these functions.
Smart homes will surely make our daily lives more convenient and comfortable.

In the future, smart homes will become even smarter and easier to use.
For example, they might sense your mood and adjust the lights and temperature to help you relax.
With the development of technology, smart homes are expected to bring more benefits to our lives.
textTranslate:

智能家居正在逐步改变人们在家中生活、学习，甚至工作的方式。

要打造一个基本的智能家居，通常首先需要一部智能手机。
接下来，将智能设备连接到互联网，并安装必要的应用程序。
一切准备就绪后，你就能更轻松地控制许多事情。

如今，许多家庭，尤其是大城市的家庭，已经在使用其中的一些功能。
智能家居一定会使我们的日常生活更加便利和舒适。

未来，智能家居会变得更加智能，也更容易使用。
例如，它们可能会感知你的情绪，并调节灯光和温度，帮助你放松。
随着科技的发展，人们期待智能家居为我们的生活带来更多益处。

title: Beacon Towers on the Great Wall
text:
When you visit the Great Wall of China, you will surely see the beacon towers.
We also call them watchtowers or guard towers because ancient soldiers kept watch for enemies from there.
Soldiers usually stayed in the towers.
If they saw enemies coming, they would make smoke during the day and light fires at night.
When the soldiers on the next tower saw the smoke or fire, they would do the same to send the signal on.
In this way, the soldiers would receive the warning quickly and get ready to fight.

People usually burned dry grass and tree branches to make smoke and fire.
In order to make sure the nearby soldiers could see the smoke clearly and easily, people usually built beacon towers on high places like mountaintops.
This added to the difficulty of building the towers, especially at a time without modern machines to help people go up the mountains.

Ancient Chinese people were clever and wise.
By building beacon towers, they could send messages over long distances.
It was like an ancient telegram system that helped protect our motherland.
textTranslate:
参观中国长城时，你一定会看到烽火台。
我们也称它们为瞭望台或警戒台，因为古代士兵会在那里监视敌人。
士兵们通常住在烽火台里。
如果他们发现敌人来袭，白天会制造烟雾，夜间会点燃火把。
当下一座烽火台上的士兵看到烟雾或火光时，他们也会这样做，以继续传递信号。
通过这种方式，士兵们能迅速收到警报，并做好战斗准备。

人们通常燃烧干草和树枝来制造烟雾和火光。
为了确保附近的士兵能清楚、容易地看到烟雾，人们通常在山顶等高地建造烽火台。
这增加了建塔的难度，尤其是在没有现代机器帮助人们登山的时代。

古代中国人聪明而睿智。
通过修建烽火台，他们能够远距离传递信息。
它就像一套古代电报系统，帮助保卫了我们的祖国。

titleTranslate: 体育为什么对我们很重要？

Almost all middle school students like physical activities which are good for their body, mind and spirit.

title: Cuju: The Oldest Form of Football
titleTranslate: 蹴鞠：最古老的足球运动形式
text:
Football is one of the most popular sports in the world.
Its history goes back over two thousand years to ancient China.
It was called cuju.
The word cu means to kick; ju is a ball made of animal skins with hair inside.
People played it by kicking the ball into a net hung in the air.

According to FIFA, cuju is the earliest form of football.
Its birthplace is Zibo, a city in Shandong Province.
It was first mentioned in the famous Chinese historical work Strategies of the Warring States and became popular during the Han Dynasty.
In ancient China, it was a fun way to exercise.
Both men and women played it.
It was also a way to train soldiers.
There were different types of cuju games.
People played it for fun, and sometimes with music.
It could also be competitive.
The players tried to score as many goals as possible to win.

As the oldest form of football, cuju is an intangible cultural heritage.
In 2005, a football museum was opened in Zibo.
textTranslate:
足球是世界上最受欢迎的运动之一。
足球的历史可以追溯到两千多年前的中国古代。
它当时被称为蹴鞠。
“蹴”意为踢，“鞠”是一种用兽皮制成、内部塞有毛发的球。
人们通过把球踢进悬挂在空中的网来玩蹴鞠。

根据国际足联的说法，蹴鞠是足球最早的形式。
蹴鞠的发源地是山东省淄博市。
它最早见于中国著名史学著作《战国策》，并在汉朝期间流行开来。
在中国古代，蹴鞠是一种有趣的锻炼方式。
男女都参与这项运动。
它也是一种训练士兵的方法。
蹴鞠比赛有不同类型。
人们以娱乐为目的玩蹴鞠，有时还配上音乐。
它也可以是一项竞技运动。
球员们试图尽可能多地进球，以赢得比赛。

作为最古老的足球运动形式，蹴鞠是一项非物质文化遗产。
2005年，淄博市了一座足球博物馆。

title: Four Brothers
text:
Once upon a time, there were four brothers.
"I can see farther than anyone," the first brother said.
"At the top of that tree, there are five eggs in a nest."
"I am faster than all of you—I move as quickly as a cat," said the second brother.
He climbed up, took the eggs quietly, and then put them back.
The bird never noticed it.
"I can shoot better than all of you," said the third.
He then shot a leaf above the nest.
The fourth brother said, "I can sew anything together, even something as soft as that leaf."
In no time, the leaf was as good as new.
Not long after, the king's daughter was taken away by a dragon.
The king said whoever brought the princess back could marry her.
The first brother said, "I see her!
She is far away, on a rock at sea, with the dragon."
So the brothers sailed to the rock.
The third brother said, "I may hurt the princess if I shoot the dragon."
"Leave it to me," said the second brother.
He moved as quietly as a mouse and quickly freed the princess.
Suddenly, the dragon began to chase them.
The third brother shot it, but its fall broke their ship.
Luckily, the fourth brother took his needle and sewed the ship together.
Then they sailed home safely.
The happy king asked, "Which of you will marry my daughter?"
The brothers began to argue.
Each brother believed that he did more than the others.
Finally, the king said, "Each of you is as good as the others, but you are much stronger together.
Instead, I give half of my kingdom to you as a reward."
The brothers were pleased.
It was much better to share than to fight.
textTranslate:
从前，有四兄弟。
大哥说：“我能看得比任何人都远。”
“那棵树的树顶上，有一个鸟巢，里面有五颗蛋。”
二哥说：“我比你们所有人都快——我跑起来像猫一样快。”
他悄悄爬上树，取走鸟蛋，然后又把它们放了回去。
那只鸟始终没有察觉。
三哥说：“我的射击比你们所有人都好。”
随后，他射中了鸟巢上方的一片叶子。
四哥说：“无论什么东西，我都能把它缝合起来 Even something as soft as that leaf.”
转眼之间，那片叶子就像新的一样完好。
不久后，国王的女儿被一条龙带走了。
国王说，谁能把公主救回来，就可以娶她。
大哥说：“我看见她了！
她在远处的海上，和龙一起待在一块礁石上。”
于是，兄弟几个驾船前往那块礁石。
三哥说：“我若向龙开枪，可能会伤害公主。”
二哥说：“交给我吧。”
他像老鼠一样悄无声息地移动，很快便救出了公主。
突然，龙开始追赶他们。
三哥射中了龙，但龙坠落后撞坏了他们的船。
幸运的是，四哥拿出针线，把船缝合好了。
然后，他们安全地扬帆回家。
快乐的国王问：“你们谁愿意娶我的女儿？”
兄弟几个开始争论起来。
每个兄弟都认为自己比其他兄弟付出的多。
最后，国王说：“你们每个人都和其他人一样优秀，但你们 together 力量强大得多。
因此，我要把一半王国赐给你们作为奖励。”
兄弟几个都很高兴。
分享比争斗好得多。

title: The Brave Homing Pigeon
text:
Somewhere in the Atlantic Ocean, 1862.
The captain sighed.
This was the thickest fog he had ever seen.
They were over 330 kilometres from the closest land, so he didn't know where to go.
The ship was on its way to Europe.
Just ten hours ago they left New York, but now the engine stopped working.
Clearly, they needed help!
Suddenly, the captain remembered the homing pigeons.
He ran to them quickly, wrote a message for help, and tied it to Big Blue's leg.
Big Blue flew up and then returned almost right away.
The captain became more worried.

"You are our last hope, little guy," said the captain as he tied a note to Arny, the smaller and younger of the two pigeons.
The captain threw him into the air.
Arny flew around and around, higher and higher.
Soon, the bird was away from the ship, and the captain couldn't see Arny anymore.
"That's a good sign," said the captain with more hope.
Almost 340 kilometres away, Billy heard fast-moving wings come into his building and go straight to the water bowl.
"Hi there, little guy.
Well, aren't you the thirstiest bird!"
Billy smiled.
Then he saw the note.
Billy knew what to do.
He took the note, running as fast as he could to the company office.
There, he learnt Arny had flown in fog and over the sea, for more than four hours.
Thanks to Arny, people sent help to the ship.
The captain later explained, "Arny really is the most amazing bird!"
textTranslate:
大西洋某处，1862年。
船长叹了口气。
这是他见过的最浓的雾。
他们离最近的陆地有330多千米，因此不知道该往哪里走。
船正在驶往欧洲。
十小时前，他们才离开纽约，但现在已经停转。
显然，他们需要帮助！
突然，船长想起了那些信鸽。
他迅速跑到信鸽那里，写了一张求助纸条，系在大蓝的腿上。
大蓝飞起来后，几乎立刻就飞了回来。
船长更加焦急了。

船长把一张便条系在阿尼的腿上——它是两只鸽子中较小、较年轻的一只——说：“小家伙，你是我们的最后希望了。”
船长把他抛向空中。
阿尼不停地盘旋，越飞越高。
不久，这只鸟便飞离了大船，船长再也看不见阿尼了。
船长满怀希望地说：“这是个好兆头。”
近340千米外，比利听见一阵疾速的振翅声飞进他的大楼，径直飞向水碗。
“你好啊，小家伙。
哇，你一定是渴坏了的小鸟！”
比利笑了。
接着，他看见了那张便条。
比利知道该怎么做。
他拿着便条，飞快地跑向公司办公室。
在那里，他得知阿尼已经在浓雾和海面上飞行了四个多小时。
多亏了阿尼，人们派人前往救助那艘船。
船长后来解释说：“阿尼真是一只了不起的鸟！”

title: Unit 3 · The History of Pizza
titleTranslate: 第3单元 · 比萨饼的历史
text:
Do you know pizza is one of the most popular fast foods in the world?
In fact, around the world, people eat 5 billion pizzas every year!
But where did pizza come from and what makes it so popular?
Read on to find out.

Thousands of years ago, the Greeks, Italians, and Persians started putting vegetables, oil, cheese, and other things on flat bread.
The ingredients depended on the area, but there was one thing in common: Everyone put the toppings on some type of bread.
This was the ancient form of "pizza".

Our modern pizza goes back to the Romans more than 2,000 years ago.
They put cheese and olive oil on bread.
In the 1700s, a pizza with tomato sauce and cheese became popular in Naples, Italy.
Later, Italians brought the pizza to America, and then it became a popular food all over the world, with different pizzas from different places.

Photographs of movie stars and famous athletes with pizza helped it become more and more popular, and that led to competitions.
Today, we have the World Pizza Games.
There are also all kinds of world records.
For example, in 2017, there was a new record for the world's longest pizza.
It was over 1.9 kilometres long!

Today, pizza is popular all over the world, and different places have their own local pizzas.
So do you like eating or cooking pizza?
What is your favourite pizza style?
textTranslate:
你知道吗？披萨是世界上最受欢迎的快餐之一。
事实上，全世界每年要吃掉50亿个披萨！
但是，披萨从何而来，又为何如此受欢迎呢？
继续阅读，了解答案。

数千年前，希腊人、意大利人和波斯人开始把蔬菜、油、奶酪及其他食材放在扁面包上。
配料因地区而异，但有一点是相同的：人们都会把各种配料放在某种面包上。
这就是披萨的古老形式。

现代披萨可以追溯到两千多年前的罗马人。
他们把奶酪和橄榄油放在面包上。
18世纪，意大利那不勒斯开始流行一种涂有番茄酱和奶酪的披萨。
后来，意大利人把披萨带到美洲，此后它便成为全世界广受欢迎的食物，各地也形成了不同的披萨。

电影明星和著名运动员手持披萨的照片帮助披萨越来越受欢迎，也由此产生了各种比赛。
如今，我们有了世界披萨大赛。
世界上还有各种各样的纪录。
例如，2017年，世界最长披萨的纪录被再次刷新。
它的长度超过了1.9千米！

如今，披萨风靡世界各地，各地都有自己独具特色的本地披萨。
你喜欢吃披萨还是做披萨？
你最喜欢哪一种披萨？

title: Unit 4 · The Ant and the Grasshopper
titleTranslate: 第4单元 · 蚂蚁和蚱蜢
text:
It was summertime.
The ant and the grasshopper were in the farmer's field.
The ant was busy collecting corn.
The grasshopper was relaxing in the sun.
"Hey, Ant, come sit with me," said the grasshopper.
"No, thanks," said the ant.
"I have to take this corn home.
I'm preparing for the winter."
A few weeks later, summer was almost at an end.
The ant continued to take corn home every day, but the grasshopper just played his violin and danced around.
"Come on, Ant!" said the grasshopper.
"Dance with me!"
"No," replied the ant.
"I'm going to get more corn.
Why don't you join me?
You should plan for the winter."
"But the winter is so far away!
Your work looks so boring!
Come with me!
Let's have a picnic!"
"No, thanks, Grasshopper.
I'm going to continue with my boring work."

The grasshopper was silent for a while, but then he happily danced away.
The ant looked tired, but she felt happy when she saw all the food in her kitchen.
The autumn arrived and the weather became cool and windy.
The grasshopper ran around the farm singing songs.
The poor ant had to fight her way through the wind.
She wanted to collect lots of wood.
"Ant, it's too windy to work!" said the grasshopper.
"Come and sing with me!"
"No, thanks, Grasshopper.
There's just a little bit more work for me to do.
I want to be warm in the winter."
And then the cold winter came.
The ant sat at home by her fire, enjoying some lovely corn soup.
Then she heard a knock at the door.
"Oh, dear Ant," said the grasshopper, "you must help me!
I have no food!
And no fire to keep me warm!"
"Sorry, Grasshopper, you must learn to look after yourself.
Keep dancing and singing through the winter, and work hard when spring comes!"

Are you curious about the future?
What do you think our life will be like in 50 years or more?
To answer this, you can read a sci-fi book.
Perhaps you will have some ideas then.
Today, many young readers are interested in science fiction.
But what makes it so popular?

For one thing, science fiction gives us a chance to imagine what our future will be like.
Anything is possible.
We can dream big.
Some people think there will be flying cars and robot servants.
Others believe we will learn more about strange aliens and other worlds.

Another reason is that sci-fi writers and their work can inspire us to create the future.
In 1945, a sci-fi author named Arthur C.
Clarke wrote about a system of space stations.
In the article, he predicted the earth of the future would have many TV stations and people would send TV programmes around the world.
However, this was before TV was a common item at home!
In a short story by Clarke, he suggested people in the future would use a system to talk with others around the world.
Amazingly, the short story was actually the inspiration for the internet!

Science fiction is also popular because it can make us think about our world in new ways.
Although many sci-fi stories are set in imaginary worlds or societies, they can help us better understand the real world.
They can also make us excited when we feel like we are living in a boring world.

What will the future be like?
Sci-fi inspires us and helps us to understand what it could be like.
textTranslate:
那是一个夏日。
蚂蚁和蚱蜢在农夫的田地里。
蚂蚁正忙着收集玉米。
蚱蜢正在阳光下休息。
“嘿，蚂蚁，来和我坐坐吧。”蚱蜢说。
“不了，谢谢。”蚂蚁说。
“我得把这些玉米带回家。
我正在为过冬做准备。”
几周后夏天就要结束了。
蚂蚁继续每天把玉米带回家，而蚱蜢却只顾着拉小提琴、四处跳舞。
“来吧，蚂蚁！”蚱蜢说。
“和我一起跳舞吧！”
“不。”蚂蚁回答。
“我要去收集更多玉米了。
你为什么不和我一起来？
你应该为过冬做好准备。”
“可是冬天还远着呢！
你的劳动看起来太无聊了！
跟我来吧！
我们去野餐吧！”
“不了，谢谢你，蚱蜢。
我要继续做我这份无聊的工作。”

蚱蜢沉默了一会儿，然后兴高采烈地跳着舞离开了。
蚂蚁看起来很疲惫，但看到厨房里堆满了食物，她感到十分开心。
秋天到了，天气变得又冷又有风。
蚱蜢在农场里四处奔跑，唱着歌。
可怜的蚂蚁不得不在风中艰难前行。
她想收集大量的木柴。
“蚂蚁，风太大了，没法干活！”蚱蜢说。
“来和我一起唱歌吧！”
“不了，谢谢你，蚱蜢。
“我还有一点点工作要做。
我想在冬天里保暖。”
寒冷的冬天随后到来了。
蚂蚁坐在家里的火炉旁，享用着美味的玉米汤。
就在这时，她听到有人敲门。
“亲爱的蚂蚁，你得帮帮我！”蚱蜢说，“你一定要救救我！
我没有食物！
也没有火让我取暖！”
“对不起，蚱蜢，你必须学会照顾自己。
整个冬天都要继续唱歌跳舞，等春天到来时就要努力劳动！”

你对未来的生活充满好奇吗？
你觉得我们的生活在50年或更久以后会是什么样子？
要找到答案，你可以阅读一本科幻小说。
也许你到时候就会有一些想法了。
如今，许多年轻读者对科幻小说感兴趣。
但科幻小说为何如此受欢迎呢？

一方面，科幻小说让我们有机会想象未来会是什么样子。
一切皆有可能。
我们可以拥有远大的梦想。
有些人认为，未来会有飞行汽车和机器人管家。
另一些人相信，我们将更多地了解奇特的外星生物和其他世界。

另一个原因是，科幻作家及其作品能够启发我们创造未来。
1945年，一位名叫阿瑟·C·克拉克的科幻作家
写了一篇关于太空站系统的文章。
在文章中，他预言未来的地球将有许多电视台，人们也会向全世界传送电视节目。
然而，那是在电视尚未普及到家庭的时候！
克拉克在一篇短篇小说中提出，未来的人们将使用一种系统与世界各地的人交谈。
令人惊叹的是，这篇短篇小说实际上启发了互联网的诞生！

科幻小说之所以受欢迎，还因为它能引导我们以新的方式思考我们的世界。
尽管许多科幻故事以虚构的世界或社会为背景，但它们能帮助我们更好地理解现实世界。
当我们觉得生活在一个无聊的世界里时，它们也能让我们感到兴奋。

未来会是什么样子？
科幻小说启发我们，帮助我们了解未来可能是什么样子。

title: Unit 6 · How to Stay Safe Online
titleTranslate: 第6单元 · 如何保障网络安全
text:
No matter whether you like it or not, social media is becoming a big part of many teenagers' lives.
The internet is popular among young people in China.
According to a survey by the Central Committee of the Communist Youth League, over 90 per cent of all Chinese minors use the internet and 50 per cent of these young people have made new friends online.

Social media allows people to connect with friends, share experiences, and stay on trend.
However, the internet also has risks.
It is important to stay safe while having fun online.
Here are some simple tips.

First, if you have accounts on different apps, make sure you use strong passwords.
Avoid using easy-to-guess information, like your birthday or your pet's name.

Second, be careful when you talk to strangers online.
Not every person online is friendly or telling the truth about themselves.
Don't share personal details, like your address, school name, or phone number.

Third, if you want to post anything online, think it over.
Once it is out there, it is hard Lastly, keep your social media profiles private so only real friends can see your posts and information.

Remember, by following these tips, you can stay safe on social media and the internet.
Your parents and teachers want the best for you.
Be aware of the risks and protect yourself.
textTranslate:
不论你喜欢与否，社交媒体正成为许多青少年生活中的一部分。
互联网在中国年轻人中很受欢迎。
据中国共产主义青年团中央委员会的一项调查，超过90%的中国未成年人使用互联网，其中50%的年轻人通过网络结交了新朋友。

社交媒体使人们能够联系朋友、分享经历并紧跟潮流。
然而，互联网也存在风险。
在网上娱乐时，确保自身安全十分重要。
下面是一些简单的建议。

第一，如果你在不同的应用程序上有账号，请务必使用强密码。
避免使用容易被猜到的信息，如你的生日或宠物的名字。

第二，在网上与陌生人交谈时要谨慎。
并非每个网上的人都是友善的或如实介绍自己的。
不要透露个人信息，如你的住址、学校名称或电话号码。

第三，如果你想在网上发布任何内容，请仔细考虑。
一旦发布出去，就很难。最后，将你的社交媒体个人资料设为私密，只有真正的好友才能看到你的帖子和信息。

请记住，遵循这些建议，你就能在社交媒体和互联网上保持安全。
你的父母和老师都希望你拥有最好的一切。
要了解风险并保护好自己。

title: Unit 7 · A Round-the-World Cycling Journey
titleTranslate: 第7单元 · 环游世界骑行之旅
text:
When planning a round-the-world trip, most people choose to take an airplane.
But what if someone decided to cycle around the world instead?
Lily, a 23-year-old newspaper reporter, did just that.

Lily grew up in a pretty town surrounded by forests and rivers.
From a young age, she was amazed by the beauty of nature and felt a deep responsibility to keep it clean and safe.
One day, while she was reporting on air pollution caused by a wildfire, she suddenly realized that it was time to do more.
She decided to ride her bicycle around the world to tell people about the importance of protecting the environment.

She went to big cities, small villages, and lots of other places.
Along the way, she saw beaches littered with plastic bags, rivers polluted by factory waste, and wild animals losing their homes.
These drove her to make a difference.
Lily worked with local communities to protect their surroundings.
She organized clean-up activities, planted trees, and taught children about recycling.
Each action she took was like a drop in a pond, creating ripples of positive changes.

Lily's journey was not without challenges.
Even though she faced many difficulties like bad weather, she didn't give up.
She knew that she was doing something very important.
And guess what?
News about Lily and her bike ride spread far and wide.
People from all over the world wanted to help too.
textTranslate:
计划环游世界时，大多数人会选择乘坐飞机。
但如果有人决定改为骑自行车环游世界呢？
莉莉是一名23岁的报纸记者，她就这样做了。

莉莉在一个被森林和河流环绕的美丽小镇长大。
从小，她就为大自然的美景惊叹，并深感有责任保护环境，使其整洁安全。
一天，她在报道一场野火造成的空气污染时，突然意识到，是时候采取更多行动了。
她决定骑自行车环游世界，告诉人们保护环境的重要性。

她去了大城市、小村庄以及许多其他地方。
一路上，她看到海滩上散落着塑料袋，河流被工厂废料污染，野生动物失去家园。
这些促使她要做出改变。
莉莉与当地社区合作，保护周边环境。
她组织清洁活动、植树，并向孩子们讲解回收利用。
她采取的每一项行动都如同一滴落入池塘的水，激起积极改变的涟漪。

莉莉的旅程并非一帆风顺。
尽管遇到了恶劣天气等许多困难，她仍没有放弃。
她知道，自己正在做一件非常重要的事。
你猜猜结果如何？
关于莉莉和她的骑行之旅的消息传遍了各地。
世界各地的人也想出一份力。
